item.summary: Just like in real life, there are some people you really shouldn’t mess with in GTA 6. It’s not always easy to tell at a glance either. Books, covers, and all that.
item.text:
Just like in real life, there are some people you really shouldn’t mess with in GTA 6. It’s not always easy to tell at a glance either. Books, covers, and all that.
GTA 6 has a wild range of NPCs with unpredictable and unique behavior — you never know what you’re gonna get. Players have been documenting their adventures across Leonida and their interactions with the locals, and have come across the weird, the funny, and the downright scary.
Not only do some NPCs fight back, but they fight hard and can take more punches to the head than Rocky. Some of them even bring little friends along to the throwdown.
The viral clip below, from @WIZZYGM, shows Lucia attempting to take someone’s car. Instead of allowing themselves to be dragged out, however, they got psyched up about having a tussle. They were into it.
Not only did they take a ridiculous number of punches directly to the nose, but at one point they even gave Lucia some free shots. Then they banged some powder up their snout and Hulked out. He even took a gunshot straight to the head!
Nah this Npc’s got it 🔥🔥🔥 #GTAVI #GTA6 #ViceCity. https://t.co/KzQt4zJOsf— WIZZY🔫⚽️ (@WIZZYGM) November 20, 2026
“I appreciate that the NPCs in this game act like true Floridians,” read one reply. “Bro said ‘I can run faster than you can drive’ nah son im turning the game off lmfaooooo,” said another.
In another clip, from @chrisdadeviant, Jason attempts to hijack a car but the person inside had a massive meltdown and started headbutting the steering wheel, honking the horn with each forehead slam. Eventually, she got out and threatened to stomp Jason’s teeth out of his head.
Jason ignored the temper tantrum and got in the car anyway, and she tried to pull him out before he drove away. Here’s the clip for that one:
😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 https://t.co/LbY0AwEJbZ— chris (@chrisdadeviant) November 20, 2026
“This is such a valid crashout lmaooooooooo,” said one fan. “Yea just let her keep the car, she clearly going through something,” another joked.
One clip going around is downright terrifying. The player, having found a sniper rifle at the top of a tower, wanted to test their aim. They looked through the scope at an NPC, took aim, and fired a shot directly at their chest.
Instead of falling over, the NPC started walking towards the tower. Blood pooled on their clothing where the bullet landed, more shots rang out and landed right on target, and they kept coming, tucking their drinks under the arm and breaking into a full sprint.

Proceed: Jason and Lucia will enter Abe's office and the final mission of the game will begin.

Proceed with $2 million in your Buck Me savings account

But one of the endings is only possible if you postpone the Protective Custody mission until you've deposited $2 million into your Buck Me savings account. That's why when you choose to proceed with the final mission makes a difference.
It's also worth noting (again, without spoilers) that just because you do have $2 million in your Buck Me savings account does not guarantee you will see this particular ending. There are still choices you'll need to make in the final mission that determine which ending you see.

But with GTA 6, which takes place in a satirized version of Florida called Leonida, players were always going to take it to another level. Thankfully, I'm here to help you understand how to get neckwear in GTA 6, how to equip masks, and how to change them for new ones.
You can buy a mask in GTA 6 from any of the gun stores. Chuck's Tackle & Shot in Key Lento sells them (look at the central stand with the alligator head atop of it) from the beginning of the game, but you can head to any Ammu-Nation retailer to find more. When you begin exploring Vice City and Vice Beach, you'll also find thrift stores that sell novelty masks, and high-end retailers which sell very fancy (and expensive) coverings that can be worn as well.

If you want options while you're on the road, you can also store some in the trunk of your personal vehicle in GTA 6 by highlighting it and pressing Square/X.
With a mask in your loadout, wearing it is as simple as holding L1/LB to open your loadout. Press R1/RB to scroll to the items menu, and then select Mask from the neckwear slot located at twelve-o'clock in the wheel. Press A to put it on, press A to remove it. But what happens when you’ve robbed an area clean? Have those locations been cleared out for the rest of time? Or do they open back up so you can repeatedly rob them? In this guide, I’ll explain how the robbery loop works in Grand Theft Auto 6.
In GTA 6, you’ll find many gang hideouts and other locations on the map, all indicated by a yellow icon that represents the gang’s insignia. These are some of the highest-value areas in the game, and they’re bursting with loot – and enemies.

The uploaded files are from an XBOX version of GTA VI, not a native PC build. Even if the missing executable becomes available, getting the game running on PC would require additional work from developers and the emulation community.

item.title: Your Xbox Can Ban You for Auto-Uploading GTA 6 Nude Clips
item.summary: A player reports a two day Xbox suspension after a GTA 6 beach clip uploaded automatically; Series X|S players can turn off automatic uploads.
item.text:
An Xbox player says their console automatically uploaded a 28-second beach clip from Grand Theft Auto VI and they immediately got a two-day suspension. The game is not the problem here. The default setting is.
On Reddit, the player described the single-player clip as showing NPCs in swimwear with no explicit nudity and said the suspension was labeled an automatic enforcement action. The player never chose to post any of it. The console did.
Each piece of this is working as designed, which is the real problem. GTA 6 carries ESRB Mature ratings with Nudity and Strong Sexual Content descriptors, the most adult rating a Grand Theft Auto game has ever received. There is no in-game toggle to switch that material off, only limited gore options unless you to happen to live in certain countrie and Xbox turns on automatic clip uploads by default. In its Community Standards, Xbox is saying sexual content does not belong in the shared community, rated game or not.
Put those three together and a clip you meant to keep private can end up subject to Xbox's rules for shared content. Sharing explicit content publicly does break the rules. The problem is that the platform is the one doing the sharing for you.
The fix, for now, is with the players. On Xbox Series X|S, go to Settings, then Preferences, then Capture and share, then set Automatically upload to Don't upload. Clips stay local until you choose to share one. None of that should be the player's job on a console that sold them the game, but it is the only switch that reliably works. The deeper issue is one we have tracked since the ratings came in. GTA 6 is built to be uncensorable, with adult content woven through the world and no master filter, the exact reason why a capture tool keeps tripping over it.
GTA 6 was always going to be defined by its adult content. Japan censored the showers and the gore, South Korea nearly refused to rate it at all over nudity and the full picture of where it is restricted keeps changing. Parents looking for control should know the console age settings gate the game itself but do not filter what happens once it is running.
Microsoft could turn off automatic uploads by default so clips stay local unless players choose to share them. Until it does, the safest move with the biggest game of the year is to stop your own Xbox from posting it for you.

item.title: Player Got Banned for 30 Days for Texting a GTA 6 Nude Screenshot
item.summary: PlayStation’s code bars obscene or pornographic material in private messages, even when it’s a screenshot from a game Sony sells.
item.text:
A Grand Theft Auto VI player says PlayStation restricted his access to social features for 30 days after he privately sent a friend a screenshot through PlayStation messages. The screenshot showed the in-game nudist colony.
An X user posted that he took a photo with the game's in-game camera at the nudist colony he found, sent it privately to an adult friend over PlayStation's messaging and got a 30-day restriction on social features. It wasn't, or isn't a full account ban yet, it was a block on the messaging and social side, flagged by an automated system that Sony upheld upon the user's request for a review.
The original post is one report. There is no wave of lost accounts, no bans for gore and no statement from Sony or Rockstar Games that says a great Grand Theft Auto purge is happening. The scale is, for all intents and purposes, small. The mechanism behind it is real though.
The mechanism is the same one that bit Xbox players. PlayStation's Community Code of Conduct bars obscene or pornographic material on its network, a rule that covers screenshots in a private message, even when the image comes straight out of a game that Sony sells. We watched the identical thing play out when Xbox suspended players for auto-uploaded GTA 6 clips. The difference is the twist. On Xbox the console uploaded the clip for you. Here the player says he sent the screenshot privately to one adult friend and still lost access to social features.
A platform has every right to moderate what crosses its network. A nudity screenshot in a message is not the same as that content sitting in your single-player game. The reason it keeps happening is the game itself. GTA 6 is built with adult content you cannot switch off and it includes nudist colony players, among other things.
An uncensorable game and a moderated network were always going to collide. After all, GTA 6 carries adult ratings in every market with no master filter, Japan censored the showers and gore, South Korea nearly refused to rate it and the map of where it is restricted keeps changing.
Seeing nudity in the game is one thing. Sending a screenshot of it through PlayStation messages can bring it under the network’s conduct rules, even if you send it privately to one friend.

item.title: GTA 6 Dunk Robbery Guide: Lost Vista Pills and Scattered Pines Crystal
item.summary: Finish Slam Dunk to get Dunk's two robbery tips, then find the pills at Lost Vista and the crystal at Scattered Pines.
item.text:
Dunk's robbery tips in GTA 6 mark two trailer parks, but they don't tell you which trailer to search. Both stashes are inside, and you can avoid most of the guards by coming around the back. We cleared Lost Vista without taking down a guard. At Scattered Pines, the back route put us behind the guard at the white trailer.
Finish Slam Dunk, then check Dunk's messages or look under Dunk's Robbery Tips on the map. Lost Vista is the pill job; Scattered Pines is the crystal job. Dunk's Trailer is the buyer marker, not a third stash. The two jobs below are separate from the car wash confrontation in Girls' Trip.
Lost Vista: Find the pills in the green-and-white trailer
Set a waypoint on Lost Vista. Go around the main entrance and approach from the muddy ground behind the trailers. Use the green trailer as your landmark, then crouch around it toward the green-and-white trailer beside it. Stay close to the trailers so you don't have to cross the main lane in front of the group.
Go inside the green-and-white trailer. Pick up two bags of pills from the table in the front room, then go through to the bedroom for the other two. When the objective changes to Leave the area, double back out the way you came in. We got the Non-Lethal result by leaving without engaging the guards.
Scattered Pines: Check the broken fridge and the back room
Select Scattered Pines on the map, south of Lost Vista. The target is the white trailer in the corner of the court. Instead of walking through the middle past the guards, go around the outside and climb the stacked wooden pallets next to the blue fence. Drop down behind the trailer by the lit steps.
Watch the guard at the back before you climb the steps. In our run, we approached him from behind while crouched and used the takedown prompt. Bring a suppressed weapon if you have one. If the second guard comes out of the trailer, deal with him at the back steps rather than trading shots across the court.
Check the broken fridge in the front part of the trailer for crystal. Then go through to the last room, where more bags sit by the old TV and on the side table by the sofa. You can ignore the wallet. Once the objective says Leave the area, return over the fence and keep going until you're outside the search area.
Leaving the search area finishes the job. You don't have to go straight to Dunk after each robbery. If you want to cash out, head to Dunk's Trailer and check his offer before selling.

The record numbers are not the only notable Grand Theft Auto story this week. In the 48 hours after Grand Theft Auto VI launched, three notable pieces of news stood out that say more about the game's reach than the $3.79 billion day did. For starters, China is buying a game it never approved. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia is playing a series it banned until last year while its wealth fund holds a stake in the publisher and, in the UK, ShopTo is already discounting the Xbox Series X|S editions.
Start with China, where GTA 6 officially does not exist. The series has never cleared the National Press and Publication Administration. It sits on no approved-import list and none of that is slowing anyone down at all. Before launch, Rockstar Games was already promoting the game on its verified Douyin account, a strange move for a game the country will not license. However, getting your hand on the game isn't exactly as dramatic as it sounds if you're China.
As Business Insider laid out, people import consoles and buy through Hong Kong or Taiwan store accounts. Shenzhen-based consultant Daniel Camilo pushed back on the workaround narrative. The platforms need no VPN, the hardware ships same-day from the mainstream retailers and he has bought games this way for most of 14 years.
Saudi Arabia is another example. The kingdom banned the series until 2025, so this is the first time players there can buy a Grand Theft Auto game legally at launch. The same country even now has money in the outcome. Reuters reports that the country's Public Investment Fund, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, holds a stake in Take-Two Interactive worth more than $2 billion, moved to its Savvy Games Group subsidiary in a February filing with the economic ownership unchanged. item.title: French Retirement Home Residents Are Trading Scrabble for GTA 6
item.summary: Jacqueline, 82, told ICI Paris Île de France her first time at the controls of a boat in GTA 6 gave her a welcome break after losing her husband.
item.text:
Residents at a French retirement home put down the Scrabble board and picked up controllers. For a game that had racked up anticipation awards and prompted questions from parents, it was a different sort of audience: about ten residents taking turns playing Grand Theft Auto VI. By the afternoon an 82-year-old who had never touched a console in her life was steering a boat through Leonida and fishing packets of cocaine out of the water.
The session ran at the Domitys residence in Serris, east of Paris, where animator Karine Gomes and her team set up a console in the main lounge as a one-off activity. About ten residents took turns playing the latest Grand Theft Auto. They stuck to the gentler corners of the game, boat trips across the Miami-inspired bay and a mission or two, while driving and shooting proved harder on arthritic hands. Nobody was speedrunning heists. They were messing about on the water in a world that happens to be GTA 6.
Jacqueline, 82, told ICI Paris Île-de-France she had never held a controller before 9 that morning and by half past two she had fished out two packets of drugs. She plans to tell her grandchildren that Mamine plays GTA VI and she is no older than they are. Then she said the part that stays with you. The game cut her off from her present life and did her a world of good, seven months after losing her husband and a finger ache was a small price.
Lucienne, 86, thought she was watching a film until someone handed her the controller. She wants one for Christmas if it is not too dear, about €80 before you count the console. She is already planning to ask her children. Gomes said a few residents found the game too violent, then defended Lucia, a woman fresh out of prison who needs money to raise her baby. A room of octogenarians arguing over a protagonist's morality is a sharper review than most of the moral-panic coverage the launch produced.

When the data said GTA 6 pulled in the everyperson, it meant this in a literal sense, a grieving widow in Seine-et-Marne who had never gamed, laughing at a boat and this grandmother who bought an Xbox to play the same game. item.title: GTA 6 Helped Turn Game Ownership Into a Political Fight
item.summary: Ahead of GTA 6’s launch without discs, Rep. Maxwell Frost proposed letting players run servers for games they bought after official servers shut down.
item.text:
The day before Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale with no disc in the box, a congressman stood at a town hall and announced a proposal aimed at keeping the games you pay for playable. The biggest launch in history was about to prove the point he was making, that buying a modern game often means renting a license the seller can revoke. The fight over game ownership we have covered all year just reached Congress.
Representative Maxwell Frost of Florida announced the Protect Our Games Act on November 18, the eve of launch, at a town hall with Stop Killing Games advocates. The idea is that a digital purchase should mean ownership, not a revocable license. It would require companies to let players run their own servers once official ones go dark, keep bought games playable as technology moves on and give advance notice before changes break access.
It's still an announcement though. It isn't a bill. Not yet, anyway. There is no text, no number and no introduction. However, Frost says it is coming early in 2027.
To make this happen, Frost is not working alone. The issue is bigger than one party. Representative Ritchie Torres of New York announced a similar Power to the Players Act in October, calling a game that vanishes when a company pulls the plug a rental disguised as a sale. California went further, its own Protect Our Games Act passed the state Assembly and carries real text, with notice rules and standalone-version requirements for games sold from 2027. Both federal efforts are Democratic so far, but owning what you buy is not a left or right idea.
The timing gave the ownership debate a high-profile example. Rockstar Games shipped GTA 6 with no disc, just a download code, turning the biggest release ever into a license rather than a thing you own. Advocates and reporters tied the announcement to that launch directly. We argued before it arrived that the game was the test case for killing physical media. The result has already pushed Sony to end PlayStation discs and lawmakers in France and Brazil to act. Washington is the latest to notice.
We are on the players' side of this. Paying full price for something a company can switch off is a bad deal. The preservation problem behind it is real. The fair counterpoint deserves airing too.
